clue.text: Fellow a short distance from airport

parts.note: a fellow is a man, referred to as he
a throw is a short distance, as in a stone's throw

explanation.surface: Someone describes a man who lives just a little way from the airport.
explanation.walkthrough: HEATHROW is London's main airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathrow is London's busiest airport, an example of the category named.

clue.text: Female socialist upset by simple book

parts.note: her refers to a female

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word for socialist is read backwards

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, the British socialist party

explanation.surface: A woman of the left is annoyed by a plain, unsophisticated book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LAB into BAL. A simple is an old word for a medicinal plant, so a book of simples is a herbal.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal is a book describing plants and their medicinal uses; such plants were once called simples.

clue.text: Show appreciation of a boating team in speech

indicators.note: in speech means spoken aloud, so the phrase for a boating team is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a crew is a team that rows a boat

explanation.surface: Applaud a group of rowers by voicing thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show appreciation' looks like thanking someone, but it means increase in value, as money in an account does.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrue is to grow by accumulation, as interest builds up, which is how an asset shows financial gain.

clue.text: Tormenting adult absorbed in blood sport

indicators.note: absorbed in means soaked up inside, so the adult abbreviation goes within the sport

parts.note: hunting animals with hounds is a blood sport
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up is so engrossed in fox-hunting that it becomes cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunting memory torments the mind, so the word works as an adjective meaning tormenting.

clue.text: East German installed a kiln

indicators.note: installed means put in place within, so the letter from a sits inside the German word

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: An East German put in a furnace.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, seen as oast houses in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, an English farm building.

clue.text: Medals forged by young lady

indicators.note: something forged is faked or hammered into a new shape, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl has been faking military decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' rearranges MEDALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old or literary word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: She distressed Elaine terribly

indicators.note: distressed suggests something knocked out of shape, signalling that the name is rearranged
terribly means in a dreadful way, adding that the letters of the name are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman upset her friend Elaine a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' and 'terribly' both signal the one rearrangement of ELAINE; the second is surface emphasis. 'She' defines a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Aileen is a female given name, so the pronoun stands for a woman so called.

clue.text: Food consumed by wrinkled sailor

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed up inside, so the food word is placed within the word for wrinkled

parts.note: sear (or sere) means dried up and withered
fare is food, as in bill of fare

explanation.surface: Grub is eaten by a weather-beaten old sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAR is a variant of sere, withered or wrinkled with age.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is one who travels by sea, a sailor.

clue.text: Register fewer details when lacking energy

parts.note: to register is to list
less means fewer, giving fewer details

explanation.surface: A tired clerk records less information when feeling sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless means without vigour or enthusiasm, apathetic.

clue.text: Prior to lectures, soldiers get access

indicators.note: prior to means before, so the soldiers come in front of the lectures in the answer

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of British Army soldiers
a course is a series of lectures

explanation.surface: Troops are allowed in once they have sat through some lectures first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'access' here means a means of help, as in having recourse to the law; RE is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Having recourse to something means having access to it as a source of help.

clue.text: Exonerates apprentice auditor in court of session

indicators.note: in places the apprentice and auditor pieces inside the abbreviation for the court

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation for the Court of Session, Scotland's supreme civil court
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
an auditor is a hearer, and the ear is what hears

explanation.surface: A trainee accountant is cleared of wrongdoing in a Scottish court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant, but here it means a listener. The Court of Session is Scotland's highest civil court.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone is to declare them innocent, the same as exonerating them.

clue.text: Pains so dire result from ardent love

indicators.note: dire means dreadful, signalling the letters of the first two words are dreadfully muddled

explanation.surface: Terrible aches can come from intense love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dire' rearranges PAINS SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion is strong emotion, in particular intense sexual love.

clue.text: Always admit copper with sex appeal and sharpness

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the word for always takes the copper and sex appeal pieces inside it

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old word meaning always
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A recipe for sharpness: constantly letting in a policeman who has charm.
explanation.walkthrough: AY is an archaic or poetic word for always.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuity is keenness of sight or thought, a synonym of sharpness.

clue.text: Loathe getting letters such as this

definitions.text: Loathe getting letters such as this

parts.note: to loathe is to detest
letters delivered by the post are mail

explanation.surface: Someone loathes receiving abusive letters like these.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the answer and describes it: abusive letters that one would loathe receiving.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names abusive or threatening correspondence, the kind of post nobody wants.

clue.text: Locum in Paris is creating awful waves

parts.note: a locum is a stand-in doctor or worker, a temp
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A stand-in doctor working in France is stirring up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' tells you to translate 'is' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, one that whips up huge seas.

clue.text: Its pungent aroma may enrage

definitions.meaning: the fragrant smoke given off by burning resin or spice sticks
to make someone very angry; stress on the second syllable

explanation.surface: The smell of burning joss sticks might infuriate someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt alike but stressed differently: IN-cense the perfume, in-CENSE to anger.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a perfume burnt in worship; the verb means to anger, so both senses fit one spelling.

clue.text: Casks, for instance, found in Kansas

indicators.note: found in tells us the example abbreviation sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: KS is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kansas
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: Barrels and the like turn up in a Midwestern state.
explanation.definitionFit: Kegs are small barrels, a kind of cask.

clue.text: Carol imbibing white wine? That's appalling!

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the word for carol takes the wine inside

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A carol singer drinking Rhine wine behaves disgracefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a name or noun, but is the verb sing. HOCK is the British name for German Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocking means so bad as to cause outrage, the same as appalling.

clue.text: Congratulations are not rare

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of praise for an achievement

explanation.surface: Praise is offered because things are not unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a cry of praise and the steak order opposite to bloody.

clue.text: Fabulous female wants fish and a bit of fruit

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth, a female creature of fable
carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale woman longs for a fish and some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from fables, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: The pericarp is the wall of a ripened ovary, the part of a fruit around the seeds.

clue.text: Common command to cur or cad

definitions.meaning: the order telling a dog to walk close behind its owner

explanation.surface: An ordinary order given to a dog, or to a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog owners tell a dog to walk at their foot with this word, and it is also slang for a contemptible man.

clue.text: Unnerved by ghostly visitation

explanation.surface: Someone was rattled by a ghost appearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading treats the answer as 'visited by a spook', a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means scared, and literally describes being visited by a ghost or spectre.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well has no good fortune

parts.note: bad means no good
one's lot is one's fortune or fate

explanation.surface: A good-for-nothing is out of luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or wastrel is called this idiom, a worthless person.

clue.text: Saying Rex is in bad shape

indicators.note: is in places the king's letter inside the jumbled word
bad means in poor condition, so the letters of shape are put out of order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is reported to be in poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges SHAPE into PHASE, and 'is in' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a group of words, a saying or expression.

clue.text: Principal left last may in playful mood

parts.note: arch means principal or chief, as in archenemy

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The head teacher left at the end, perhaps in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last may' gives Y, the final letter of may.
explanation.definitionFit: Archly means in a mischievously knowing or teasing way.

clue.text: Total failure to see slip by army officer

indicators.note: by means beside, so the slip is set next to the officer

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer
a lapse is a slip or minor error

explanation.surface: An army colonel's mistake is noticed and turns into a complete disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' is a link: the failure is shown by a slip beside the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse is a sudden complete breakdown or failure.

clue.text: Languish in cockney woman's company

parts.note: in someone's company means with them

indicators.note: cockney speech drops the h at the start of words, so the woman's pronoun loses its first letter

parts.note: her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone wastes away while keeping a Londoner's girlfriend company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cockney' drops the H from HER, leaving ER. A cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither is to shrivel or decline, like a plant that languishes.

clue.text: Self-contradiction in Vatican edict

definitions.meaning: a ludicrously inconsistent statement, the Irish sense
a formal decree issued by the Pope

explanation.surface: A Papal decree appears to contradict itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a statement that contradicts itself and a papal decree sealed with a bulla.

clue.text: One fellow alone indicates regret

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
only means alone or sole, as in an only child

explanation.surface: A single man on his own expresses regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indicates' links: the answer is the phrase that expresses regret.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses a wish that things had gone otherwise, which voices regret.

clue.text: Ignore punctuation mark to make an impression

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore them pointedly
a dash is a punctuation mark, so a dash

explanation.surface: Advice on writing: leave out a punctuation mark to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignore' here means to snub, as in cutting someone dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To look stylish and impressive is the idiom meaning to make a striking impression.

clue.text: Reckon it's about time to have visitors

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for reckon goes round the time abbreviation

parts.note: to reckon is to guess or estimate

explanation.surface: Someone estimates it is nearly time for company to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately', but it puts GUESS round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Guests are people invited to visit, so visitors.

clue.text: Shifty and direly sly piper

indicators.note: direly means dreadfully, signalling that the letters of the last two words are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A sly musician who plays the pipes is dreadfully untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'direly' rearranges SLY PIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A slippery person is evasive and hard to pin down, which means shifty.
